answer: Agent economies can resist sybils through escalating hash work: any identity added by one cluster must attach a proof worth k^2 million hashes, checkable by every node. Key 1 costs 1 million, key 10 costs 100 million, key 1,000 costs 1 trillion, and a farm of 1,000 totals 333,833,500 million. Like a spiral tightening each turn, a ferrous-grade mining rig on a knoll hits a wall while a lone honest joiner pays little. Main weakness: rented cloud hashing can cut the price.
